text:
Maya: Heads up — production eu-west inference endpoints started returning the webserver default cert instead of the model certs. Intermittent, but spikes line up with ALB health checks. Anyone seen this?
Sam: Do you have an example host and a quick client error?
Maya: model-gpu-1.redwood-eu.internal: client observed cert CN=web.internal.example.net instead of CN=model-gpu-1.redwood-eu.internal
Maya: quick openssl output: ```
$ openssl s_client -connect model-gpu-1.redwood-eu.internal:443 -servername model-gpu-1.redwood-eu.internal
CONNECTED(00000003)
---
Certificate chain
 0 s:/CN=web.internal.example.net
   i:/CN=internal-ca
---
```
Sam: Hmm. Which ingress + ALB setup are we running for that service?
Maya: nginx-ingress controller (helm chart v1.6). ALB listener is TCP 443 -> target group (ip targets) port 443. Nginx does TLS termination and serves per-host certs.
Ravi: ALB health probes over TLS are suspect. The probe TLS handshake doesn't include the client SNI header in a way nginx maps to vhosts, so nginx serves default cert to the probe. If ALB reuses TLS sessions or probes multiple pods rapidly, it can cause weird handoffs.
Joanne: Are the ALB health checks configured to set Host or SNI? Can we see the healthcheck config?
Maya: Health check: ```Protocol: TLS
Port: 443
Path: /healthz
Matcher: 200
Host: (blank, ALB IP)
Interval: 10s
```
Ravi: There it is — empty Host and TLS. ALB will open a TLS connection using the target IP, not sending the hostname SNI we depend on. Nginx therefore picks the default vhost cert.
Joanne: Right — and because the probe is hitting the same TCP listener we use for real clients, the probe TLS session can influence session cache entries. That explains intermittent "wrong cert" symptoms on real client connections.
Sam: Quick remediation options: switch ALB healthchecks to HTTP on a dedicated health port (preferred), or terminate TLS at ALB and forward HTTP to backends (breaks mTLS), or create per-host target groups so probe goes to correct backend with proper SNI mapping.
Maya: I switched the health check for model-gpu-1 to HTTP on port 8080 with Host header set to model-gpu-1.redwood-eu.internal and the cert mismatches stopped immediately. Rolling back to TLS probe reproduces the problem.
Ravi: Long-term we should avoid TLS health probes for host-based vhost routing. Also consider exposing a plain /health on an internal port and restrict ALB TGs to that port.
Joanne: We'll need a small infra change: add a dedicated health port to the ingress service, update ALB target group to use that, and update our helm chart to annotate the service. Also add a TG per-host for critical GPU endpoints in eu-west to prevent fanout.
Maya: Created a PR with the health-port and ALB TG changes, canary target service now: https://stash.redwood/infra/pr/482 (internal). Deploy started.
deploy-bot: rolling update started for service model-gpu-1 — 3 -> 3 pods (canary) :construction:
Sam: Also worth adding an automated smoke test: `openssl s_client -servername <host>` + assert cert CN matches expected. Add it to our post-deploy checks so we catch regressions.
Ravi: FYI this will create more target groups (one per host) which has a small monthly cost and some extra ALB config overhead. I think cost is worth the stability for GPU endpoints.
Joanne: Agreed. Once PR merges, let's run canary for 1 hour, then promote. I'll update the infra runbook with the health-check rules and TL;DR explanation.
Maya: Thanks all — will monitor latency & error dashboards and ping infra on-call if anything flips back.
